items.stem: Why is the C++ memory model and choice of memory order important when using std::atomic?

options.text: It defines which reorderings are allowed, so incorrect ordering can cause subtle data races or stale reads
options.rationale: Correct: memory order constrains visibility and reordering; getting it wrong breaks correctness in ways that are hard to reproduce.

options.text: It makes atomics slower but never affects correctness
options.rationale: Ordering directly affects correctness, not merely speed.

options.text: It is only relevant on single-core machines
options.rationale: It matters specifically on multi-core, concurrent execution.
Atomics take a memory-order argument that governs their guarantees.

items.explanation: Correct: memory order constrains visibility and reordering; getting it wrong breaks correctness in ways that are hard to reproduce.

items.stem: Which claims about optimisation in C++ are sound? (Select TWO)

options.text: Profile first to find the actual hot path before optimising
options.rationale: Correct: measurement prevents wasting effort on code that does not matter.

options.text: Improving data cache locality can beat micro-optimising instructions
options.rationale: Correct: memory-access patterns often dominate performance on modern CPUs.
volatile does not provide atomicity or ordering; atomics or locks do.

options.text: Marking everything inline always makes code faster
options.rationale: Over-inlining can bloat code and hurt the instruction cache.

items.explanation: Correct: measurement prevents wasting effort on code that does not matter.; Correct: memory-access patterns often dominate performance on modern CPUs.

items.stem: What is the benefit of CRTP (the curiously recurring template pattern) over runtime polymorphism here?

options.text: It provides compile-time polymorphism, avoiding virtual-call and vtable overhead on a hot path
options.rationale: Correct: CRTP resolves the call at compile time, removing virtual dispatch cost where it matters.

options.text: It makes the class usable without templates
options.rationale: CRTP is a template technique, not a way to avoid templates.

options.text: It replaces the need for a destructor
options.rationale: CRTP does not change resource management.

items.explanation: Correct: CRTP resolves the call at compile time, removing virtual dispatch cost where it matters.
